extracted.intended_audience: ML/AI practitioners, model developers, software engineers integrating models, policymakers, auditors, and other stakeholders who release or evaluate trained machine learning models
extracted.subtask_description: Create short (one- to two-page) model cards that document a trained machine learning model’s characteristics, intended uses, disaggregated evaluation results, and ethical considerations to inform stakeholders and support responsible deployment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model Details
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide person or organization developing model; model date; model version and how it differs from previous versions; model type (e.g., Naive Bayes, CNN) including architecture and assumptions; information about training algorithms, parameters, fairness constraints or other applied approaches, and features; paper or other resource for more information; citation details; license; where to send questions or comments about the model. Note: do not force disclosure of proprietary or sensitive details; disclose basic decisions and facts that can be shared without compromising private information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended Use
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear statement of envisioned use cases, users, and out-of-scope uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List primary intended uses (broad or narrow), primary intended users (e.g., enterprise, hobbyists, younger audiences), and out-of-scope uses (disclaimers/warning-label style). Provide examples (e.g., 'not for use on text examples shorter than 100 tokens', 'for black-and-white images only'). Use this section to frame the statistical analyses and explain contexts for which the model was developed or is inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors (Relevant and Evaluation Factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: The salient conditions under which model performance may vary, including groups, instrumentation, and environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe Relevant factors: foreseeable salient factors for which model performance may vary and how they were determined. Describe Evaluation factors: which factors are being reported and why; if different from relevant factors, explain why. Include groups (cultural, demographic, phenotypic — unitary and intersectional; guidance on labels: prefer self-identified labels or clearly labelled perceived labels; document who annotated labels, annotator instructions, compensation, inter-annotator agreement). Include instrumentation (hardware/software used to capture inputs: camera type, lens, recording settings) and environment (lighting, humidity, other deployment conditions). Consider privacy and legal constraints when inferring/storing sensitive group labels; collaborate with policy/privacy/legal experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose and justify metrics that reflect the model’s structure and intended real-world impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which model performance measures are reported and why they were selected. Report decision thresholds and justify them; when possible provide interactive threshold exploration (e.g., threshold slider). Describe approaches to uncertainty and variability (standard deviation, variance, confidence intervals, bootstrap resampling, number of runs/cross-validation). For classification systems, report confusion-matrix-derived metrics (false positive rate, false negative rate, false discovery rate, false omission rate) and explain context-dependent importance; list all values and provide context about which were prioritized and why. Explain how parity of particular metrics across groups maps to fairness definitions (e.g., equal FNR = Equality of Opportunity; equal FNR and FPR = Equality of Odds). For score-based systems, report distributional summaries (mode, median, mean), dispersion measures (range, quartiles, absolute deviation, variance, standard deviation), and other distributional comparison measures (cross entropy, perplexity, KL divergence, pinned AUC). Note that some tasks (translation, speech recognition) can be analyzed via score differences (BLEU, word-error-rate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence and Uncertainty Quantification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide measures of statistical confidence and describe how uncertainty/variability were estimated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report confidence intervals for reported metrics when possible (e.g., 95% CI calculated with bootstrap resampling). Explain how confidence intervals are computed (e.g., treating confusion matrices as probabilistic models). State how many runs or cross-validation folds were used (e.g., average of 5 runs, 10-fold cross-validation). Make clear how uncertainty interacts with disaggregated analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Details about datasets used for quantitative analyses and the rationale for selection and preprocessing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which datasets were used to evaluate the model; why these datasets were chosen; preprocessing steps applied for evaluation (tokenization, cropping, filtering). Prefer evaluation datasets that are publicly available for third-party verification, or provide accompanying evaluation datasets. Ensure evaluation datasets represent typical use cases, anticipated test scenarios, and challenging cases; consider providing multiple evaluation sets (one matching expected deployment population and another containing more challenging examples). When real datasets lack representation, consider synthetically generated datasets (e.g., template-based identity phrase tests) while noting limitations of synthetic data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Data
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about the data used to train the model, or minimal allowable summaries if full disclosure is infeasible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, mirror Evaluation Data section with details on training datasets: datasets used, motivation, preprocessing, and distributions over factors/groups. If full details are not possible (proprietary data, NDAs), provide minimal information such as distributions over groups and other high-level characteristics that inform likely biases encoded by the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative Analyses (Disaggregated Results)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disaggregated (unitary and intersectional) quantitative evaluation results using chosen metrics and factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide unitary results: model performance with respect to each factor. Provide intersectional results: performance for intersections of evaluated factors (e.g., age+race). Present metric variation visually and numerically with error bars and confidence intervals. Report results at specified decision thresholds (e.g., .5) and explain threshold choice; consider reporting across thresholds. Explain how parity/variance across groups relates to fairness considerations. Include details on how metrics were computed (bootstrap, probabilistic interpretation, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative of ethical analyses, mitigations, known risks, and decisions made during model development and release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss whether the model uses any sensitive data (protected classes), whether the model is intended to inform decisions central to human life or flourishing (health, safety), mitigation strategies used during development, identified risks and harms (recipients, likelihood, magnitude), and use cases that are especially fraught. Note reviews by external boards or testing with specific communities where applicable. Include values guiding work (e.g., transparency, inclusivity, privacy) and how privacy constraints affected modeling choices (e.g., not using user history).

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveats and Recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations, unresolved concerns, and concrete recommendations for model use and future testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List additional concerns not covered elsewhere: groups not represented in evaluation data, further recommended testing, suggestions for model use, and ideal characteristics of an evaluation dataset for this model. Highlight limitations of synthetic test data if used. Recommend remedial actions (e.g., fine-tuning with underrepresented groups) and complementary transparency practices such as third-party algorithmic audits, adversarial testing, and inclusive user feedback mechanisms. Emphasize that model cards should be updated with each model release and that their usefulness depends on the integrity of their creators.
